findings.explanation: retry_config defaulted to retry_count = 0 and max_retry_duration = "0s" (variables.tf:107-113), wired straight through into the job's retry_config block (google_cloud_scheduler_job.tf:19-25). A single transient failure of the Cloud Function invocation (cold start timeout, brief 5xx, IAM propagation delay) was never retried. Combined with the default daily schedule ("0 0 * * *"), a failed run wasn't attempted again for up to 24 hours.
findings.fix_applied: Module default changed to retry_count = 3, max_retry_duration = "600s" (variables.tf:107-113). This changes the module's default behavior for existing callers that rely on the old zero-retry default and don't override retry_config.
findings.note: Also caught deterministically going forward by HLD_GCP_455 (submitted, see suggested_policies_status below).
findings.remediation: Set a non-zero retry_count and a matching max_retry_duration.
findings.title: Cloud Scheduler job has zero retries on transient failure

findings.explanation: min_instance_count defaulted to 1 (variables.tf:180-188), which kept a billed instance warm continuously. The module's only wired trigger, google_cloud_scheduler_job.invoke_cloud_function, defaults to schedule = "0 0 * * *" (once daily, variables.tf:40-48). Paying for an always-warm instance to avoid cold-start latency made little sense for a target invoked once a day.
findings.fix_applied: Module default changed to min_instance_count = 0 (variables.tf:180-188). Callers that genuinely need a warm instance (HTTP-triggered, latency-sensitive) should now pass min_instance_count explicitly. This changes default behavior for existing callers relying on the old always-warm default.
findings.remediation: Default min_instance_count to 0 so the module scales to zero between invocations.
findings.title: Function kept warm 24/7 by default while its only trigger fires once a day

findings.explanation: length(...) >= 0 can never be false, so these validation blocks never reject any input: env_vars (variables.tf:82-85), secrets (variables.tf:174-177), vpc_connector (variables.tf:228-231, using trimspace(...) >= 0 which has the same problem).
findings.fix_applied: env_vars: keys must match a valid env-var-name regex. secrets: key/secret/version must be non-empty. vpc_connector: must not have leading/trailing whitespace.
findings.remediation: Replaced each no-op validation with a real constraint instead of deleting outright, since holden's own HLD_TF_021 (variables should have validation rules) flagged the bare deletion.
findings.title: Three variable validations are tautologically true and check nothing

already_covered_by.note: An existing, unconditional holden policy (google_storage_bucket.lifecycle_rule not_null) already covers this exact gap. It never fired in earlier repo-wide scans because example/examplea is a separate self-contained Terraform root (own terraform.tf/provider) and `holden scan .` does not descend into it automatically -- confirmed via a direct `holden scan example/examplea`, which surfaces 411+ checks not counted in the root scan's ~289. Future best-practices/AI-review runs on this repo should scan example/examplea as an explicit second target.

findings.explanation: versioning.enabled = true (google_storage_bucket.bucket.tf:13-15) with no lifecycle_rule. This bucket stores the function's deployment archive, which the module replaces under a new random-suffixed name on every source change (google_storage_bucket_object.archive.tf). Deleting the old-named object in a versioned bucket doesn't remove it — it becomes a noncurrent version that's retained (and billed) forever without a lifecycle rule to purge it.
findings.remediation: Add a lifecycle_rule to expire noncurrent versions.
findings.title: Example bucket has object versioning enabled with no lifecycle rule to expire noncurrent versions

findings.explanation: output_file_mode = "0666" let any local user or process modify the deployment zip between creation and upload. Deterministically caught by holden's HLD_TF_068.
findings.title: Archive file created with world-writable permissions

findings.explanation: No soft_delete_policy.retention_duration_seconds set. Deterministically caught by holden's HLD_GCP_385 (requires >= 604800).
findings.remediation: Add a soft_delete_policy block with a 7-day (or greater) retention.
findings.title: Example bucket missing soft-delete retention

findings.explanation: The module's kms_key_name variable (used for the storage bucket object's own KMS encryption, added in commit 6efbe26) has no default and wasn't wired through from the example, so `tofu validate` failed with 'kms_key_name is required' -- the example was broken before this session touched it.
findings.fix_applied: kms_key_name = google_kms_crypto_key.pike.id (reusing the same key already used for the function's encryption in this example).
findings.remediation: Pass kms_key_name in the module call.
findings.title: Example root doesn't pass the required kms_key_name argument, breaking tofu validate/apply

suggested_policies_status.note: Not yet reflected in the installed holden CLI (go bin) -- it currently tops out at HLD_GCP_454. Will only show up in local scans after the PR merges and the CLI is rebuilt/reinstalled from source.
suggested_policies_status.title: Cloud Scheduler jobs should retry on failure
